operations.name: stock.item.create
operations.idempotencyKey: name + category + branch, so a double press does not leave two items for one shelf
operations.purpose: Create a stock item with its unit, reorder level and type.

parameters.name: name
parameters.notes: 2 to 100 characters, unique within its category (BR-6, E1). Two entries for the same thing is two balances for one shelf.

parameters.name: category_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No such category. Who maintains the category list, and whether one may be created while creating an item, is an open question this use case raises and does not answer (OQ-1).
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the categories that match.

parameters.notes: What kind of item it is. Lists and counts group by it.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.notes: The unit the item is counted in (E2). **Fixed once anything moves against the item** — changing it would make every past receipt, issue and count mean something different from what it meant when it was recorded (BR-2, E5, AC-5).

parameters.name: reorder_level
parameters.notes: Zero or more (E3). The quantity at which the item must be bought again. A standing commitment to buy rather than a description, which is why only the School Admin sets it (BR-3, E4, AC-4).

parameters.name: item_type
parameters.notes: A consumable is used up once issued. A returnable is expected back and **stays outstanding against the person who took it** until it is returned (BR-4, AC-6, AC-7). Never guessed from the item's name.

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: The item and what it now permits.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: name
fields.description: As entered, unique within its category.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: What it is counted in, from here on and permanently (BR-2).

fields.name: reorder_level
fields.description: The level at which it is flagged for buying (BR-7).

fields.name: item_type
fields.description: Consumable or returnable, which decides whether an issue of it ever closes (BR-4).

fields.name: on_hand
fields.description: Zero. The quantity comes from receipts, issues and counts and is never typed (BR-5, E6).

fields.name: available_for
fields.description: Requests, receipts, issues and counts (AC-1).

errors.meaning: An item of the same name already exists in that category.
errors.note: Two entries called the same thing in one category is how a store ends up with two balances for one shelf (BR-6, AC-2).
It is what triggers buying the item again (BR-3, AC-3).

errors.meaning: A member of staff attempted to set the reorder level.
errors.note: A reorder level commits the school to buying, so it sits with the School Admin and not with whoever holds the store (BR-3, AC-4).

planningRules.rule: Never guess the unit. It is fixed the moment anything moves against the item and cannot be changed afterwards by any route (BR-2, E5, AC-5) — a marker counted in boxes and a marker counted in pieces are the same shelf and two different balances. Ask which.

Never guess consumable or returnable. It decides whether an issue of the item ever closes: a returnable stays outstanding against the person who took it, a consumable does not (BR-4, AC-6, AC-7). A projector remote read as a consumable is an item nobody is ever asked to bring back.
Never set or suggest a reorder level of your own. It is a standing commitment to buy, it belongs to the School Admin, and a level nobody chose is a purchasing decision nobody made (BR-3, BR-8, E4).
Never offer to set the quantity on hand. There is no such field — the balance comes from receipts, issues and counts (BR-5, E6, AC-9).

Check the name against the category before creating. A near-duplicate is refused only on an exact match, and "Marker, black" beside "Whiteboard marker, black" passes the check and splits the shelf in two (BR-1, BR-6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: An item created in error is deactivated with a reason and stays readable, because receipts, issues and counts reference it (BR-9, E8). There is no deletion. An item with the wrong unit cannot be corrected at all once it is in use — it is deactivated and a new one created, so past counts keep their meaning (A4).

parameters.name: reorder_level
parameters.notes: The new level. Only the School Admin may set it, and the change is recorded with who made it — a level that moved without explanation is a purchasing decision nobody made (BR-3, BR-8, E4, A5).

parameters.name: item_type
parameters.notes: Where the item was recorded as the wrong kind. Changing it changes what happens to every future issue, not to the ones already out (BR-4).

parameters.name: branch_id

fields.name: changed

fields.name: unit
fields.description: Unchanged, always. It is not a parameter of this operation (BR-2).

fields.name: open_issues_affected
fields.description: Returnable issues already outstanding against people. A change of type does not close them or open them — it applies from here on (BR-4, BR-5).

errors.meaning: A change to the unit was attempted on an item already in use.
errors.note: It has receipts and issues against it, and changing the unit would make them mean something different (BR-2, AC-5). The route is deactivating it and creating a new item (A4).

errors.meaning: The new name already exists in that category.
A member of staff attempted to change the reorder level.
errors.note: A reorder level commits the school to buying (BR-3, AC-4).

planningRules.rule: Never attempt the unit. It is not a parameter here and it cannot be changed by any route once the item is in use — say so plainly and name the alternative: deactivate this item and create a new one, so past counts keep the meaning they had (BR-2, E5, A4).

Say who a reorder-level change binds. It is a standing commitment to buy, it is recorded with the name of whoever moved it, and it takes effect the moment the balance crosses it (BR-3, BR-7, BR-8, A5).

Say what a change of type does not do. Turning a consumable into a returnable does not open the issues already made, and turning a returnable into a consumable does not close the ones outstanding — it applies from here on, and the items already out stay exactly as they were (BR-4, BR-5).
Never correct a balance here. The quantity on hand is not editable on this screen or any other; a shelf that disagrees with the system is settled by a count (BR-5, E6).

reversal.statement: There is no undo. A further change is another change and both rows stay in the history, which is the point — a reorder level that moved without explanation is a purchasing decision nobody made (BR-8).

planningRules.rule: Say where the quantity on hand comes from. It is arithmetic over receipts, issues and counts — not a measurement — and an item nobody has counted has a balance nobody has confirmed (BR-5, AC-9).
Give the shortfall, not only the flag. "Below reorder level" says an item needs buying; 4 on hand against a level of 20 says how badly, and the two read the same on a screen (BR-7, AC-8).

Separate what is on the shelf from what is out. A returnable item shows a low balance because people are holding it, not because the school is short of it, and buying more is the wrong answer to that (BR-4).
Never suggest editing a balance that looks wrong. There is no such field; the answer is a count (BR-5, E6).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing, so there is nothing to reverse.

request.text: kaunse items reorder level se neeche hain?
request.gloss: which items are below their reorder level?

steps.note: Only active items — a deactivated one cannot be requested anyway (PR-1 covers where the figure comes from).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each item with its shortfall against the level, not just the list. Then two things the screen does not separate: any returnable item here is low because people are holding it rather than because the school is short, and any item never confirmed by a count has a balance that is arithmetic rather than a fact.

request.text: store mein A4 paper kitna para hai?
request.gloss: how much A4 paper is there in the store?

steps.note: One read; the answer is a single item's balance.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the figure in reams, which is how this item is counted, and say when it was last confirmed by a count. If it never has been, say so — the number is what receipts and issues add up to, and the shelf is the only place that settles it.

routesElsewhere.note: This is the record of changes to the item's own definition — its name, category, reorder level and type. What moved in and out of the store is the receipt and issue record.

steps.note: One read of an append-only record. Nothing in it can be edited (BR-8).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. An item that cannot be identified returns no history, since the history of the wrong item is worse than none.
plan.atomicity: A read. The record is append only — a change adds a row and never rewrites one (BR-8).

operations.name: stock.item.history.read
operations.purpose: Return every change made to an item's definition, with the previous value and who made it.

parameters.name: item_id

resolves.onNoMatch: Refuse. No item matches, active or deactivated.
resolves.onAmbiguous: Ask, naming the items that match with their category and unit.

parameters.notes: The item, including one already deactivated — its history stays readable (BR-9).

parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

returns.description: Everything that has been changed about the item.

fields.name: item_id
fields.description: The item.

fields.name: changes
fields.description: When, which field, from what to what, and who changed it (BR-8).

fields.name: reorder_level_changes
fields.description: Set apart, because each one is a standing decision to start buying at a different point and it binds the school until somebody moves it again (BR-3, A5).

fields.name: type_changes
fields.description: Changes between consumable and returnable. Each applies from that moment on and did nothing to the issues already outstanding (BR-4).

fields.name: created
fields.description: Who created the item and when, with the unit they fixed.

fields.name: deactivation
fields.description: When it was deactivated, by whom and the reason given (BR-9).

errors.meaning: The acting user cannot see the item history.
errors.note: The history screen is open to the School Admin and the Principal.

planningRules.rule: Give the reorder-level changes as decisions, not as edits. Each one changed the point at which the school starts buying, and the name against it is the person who decided that (BR-3, BR-8, A5).

Say what a change of type did and did not do. It applied from that moment on; the issues already outstanding were untouched, so a returnable turned consumable left items out with nobody expected to bring them back (BR-4, BR-5).
Name the unit as the thing that never changed. It was fixed at creation and no row will ever show it moving, which is what makes every past count readable (BR-2).
branch_id comes from $session.

reversal.statement: A read changes nothing. The record it reads cannot be edited by anybody, which is what makes it worth reading.

request.text: A4 paper ka reorder level kis ne aur kab badla tha?
request.gloss: who changed the reorder level on A4 paper and when?

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give each change with the level before and after, the date and the name. Say plainly that a level moved from 10 to 25 means the school now starts buying fifteen reams earlier every time, and that it has bound the school since that date without anything else being decided.

request.text: ye item kab aur kyun band kiya gaya tha?
request.gloss: when and why was this item deactivated?

steps.note: A deactivated item has a history like any other — that is why it was never deleted (PR-3 names the unit; the record itself is complete).

resolvedPlans.outcome: Give the date, the name and the reason as it was written. Add what the record also shows: what was on the shelf when it went out of use, since that stock did not disappear and still appears in a physical count.
